data.narrative:
Vast is a late-stage Space & Aerospace company that has raised over $300M to date. The valuation landscape includes five public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) with a median P/S multiple of 23.9x, and eight private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, Impulse Space, and Apex Space.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis, using the $300M+ total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical 1.2x step-up multiplier for late-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $360M. The peer-median approach could not be executed due to insufficient comparable datapoints at the same or adjacent stage; while 11 same-sector private peers exist, none met the narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) required for a reliable median. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable without disclosed revenue figures, a standard limitation when valuing private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $306M to $414M, with $360M as the central point. This range reflects the stage-progression method's mechanical application but carries material uncertainty around Vast's actual revenue, profitability trajectory, and competitive position relative to both public and private peers. Any refinement would require disclosure of financial performance or a larger, more granular peer dataset at comparable stages.
